Dataset group with datasets: item interactions (the core data), items (metadata such as category or price), users (metadata such as age band), and actions for next-best-action use cases. Import historical data in bulk from S3 and record new events in real time with an event tracker (PutEvents).

Domain dataset groups (for example ecommerce or video on demand) offer recommenders optimized for common use cases. Custom dataset groups let you choose a recipe, such as User-Personalization-v2, Similar-Items, Personalized-Ranking-v2, or Trending-Now, and train a solution.

Serving: a campaign (or a recommender) serves real-time recommendations through an APIAPI (Application programming interface)A defined way for one program to ask another for data or actions, such as a set of HTTPS requests and responses. Every AWS service is controlled through its API, which the console, the CLI, and the SDKs call for you.Glossary entryClose; batch inference jobs produce recommendations for many users at once (for example for emails); batch segment jobs produce user segments.
Filters exclude or include items by rules, such as removing items a user has already bought or showing only items in stock.

Cold startCold startThe extra delay when AWS Lambda must create a new execution environment, load the code, and run its initialization before handling a request. Later requests reuse the environment and are faster; provisioned concurrency avoids cold starts.Glossary entryClose: new items and users are handled through metadata and exploration of new items, so they can be recommended before they have many interactions.
Re-ranking search results: Personalize can re-rank results from Amazon OpenSearch Service for each user.
Recommended for you, real time→ leads to Campaign or recommender
Recommendations in tomorrow's emails→ leads to Batch inference job
Users likely to buy a category→ leads to Batch segment job
Hide items already purchased→ leads to Filter
Learn from clicks as they happen→ leads to Event tracker (PutEvents)
Own recommender algorithm with full control→ leads to SageMaker AI
Personalize turns interaction data into real-time and batch recommendations, rankings, and segments.
Datasets: interactions, items, and users; event trackers stream new interactions.
Use domain recommenders for common cases, or custom recipes and solutions; serve with campaigns or batch jobs.
Filters apply business rules; metadata helps with cold start.

Amazon Personalize is a fully managed machine learningML (Machine learning)Software that learns patterns from example data to make predictions or decisions, instead of following rules written by hand. A model is first trained on data, then used to make predictions on new data, which is called inference.Glossary entryClose service that uses your data to generate item recommendations for users (such as "Recommended for you", "Frequently bought together", or "More like this"), re-rank lists for each user, and create user segments for marketing. It trains models on item interaction data (clicks, views, purchases), optionally with item and user metadata, and serves results in real time or in batches. No ML expertise is needed to start.

Choose Personalize when a question asks for personalized recommendations or rankings without building a recommender model yourself (MLA-C02 tasks 2.1.4 and 2.1.8). Build your own model in SageMaker AI only when you need algorithms or control that Personalize doesn't offer.
IAM controls access; datasets and models are encrypted with KMS keys; Personalize reads data from S3 through a role you grant; CloudTrail logs API calls.
A managed service; retrain solution versions regularly, or use automatic training, so recommendations follow changing behaviour.
Campaigns have a minimum provisioned throughput (transactions per second) and scale above it; use batch jobs for bulk outputs instead of many real-time calls.

Pay for data ingested, training hours, and recommendation requests (real-time throughput or batch volume); there is no minimum fee. Keep campaign minimum throughput low and use batch for offline work.

CloudWatch metrics for campaigns and recommenders; offline metrics (such as precision and coverage) for each solution version to compare models; A/B test recommendations with your own tools or partners.
